candidates.title: Terraformers review
candidates.text: The map you're on. The cards you draw. The resources that surround you. This mechanic called "expectations" which, if it gets out of control, will be ultimately what ends your game. So you have to frantically build ahead of these expectations and hope you get the right cards, have the right resources nearby to make this all happen.The roguelike element helps to unlock more cards but that's in and of itself a bit of an issue because it keeps you from getting the cards that you really need. In my first game, I couldn't draw a card to increase power to save my life. No power = no exploration. No exploration = no expansion. No expansion = can't stay ahead of expectations. The second game was similar but with orbital options, which cuts out a lot of specialty things. The game is hard. I didn't come close to winning even the very first scenario. And while I'd like to try an easier, more relaxed version of this there seems to be no difficulty settings. Card game + roguelike + difficult with no settings = not for me. If you want a roguelike card game based in space I'm sure you could do a lot worse. If you're looking for a strategy city builder then this isn't the game you're looking for.

candidates.title: Terraformers review
candidates.text: 我觉得还不错，算是近期把rougelike元素和回合制种田结合得比较好的游戏。事件分布也比较有节奏感，每一个“下一回合”都充满着期待。但瑕疵还是有的，一些bug部分不谈。只谈设计方面的问题。由于游戏在区域和卡牌上有着双重随机要素，使得开局非常吃运气成分。例如在初始区域就有水、硝酸盐等前期发展所需资源，则前期扩张速度会远远高于没有这些资源的开局。而卡牌抽取则影响了建筑规划，前期卡牌不合理可能直接卡死扩张速度。而后期则有可能产生部分资源过剩却无法发展的困境。我是遇到过粮食堆积超过200，但愣是完全抽不到人口建筑和机器人建筑，导致根本无法扩张的情况。这使得其他资源也堆积着无法建造。个人建议是在游戏中加入每回合可以重新抽取一次卡牌机会的科技建筑或者可以定向产出所需卡牌的科技建筑来降低由运气带来的运营困境。如果游戏中已经有而我还没解锁的话，可略过这一条。另外也建议增加一些可以将积压资源快速转换成其他资源的方式，即使是亏损一定资源，以此规避某些资源产出过剩，而另一些极其紧缺的问题。虽然这个问题可以通过规划来规避，但由于地块和卡牌所需资源的随机性以及后期资源增长速度远高于贸易。使得某些资源大量囤积而花不出去。例如出现3位数硝酸盐与1位数硅酸盐的情况。如果游戏能把运气成分和规划成分再调整一下的话，会非常有趣味。否则一味通过不停调高满意度来逼迫玩家这并不合理。

candidates.title: Terraformers review
candidates.text: 无论是前期、中期还是后期，各阶段玩家的各项资源都是稀缺的。 资源类型很多，包括粮食、电力、科学、水、硝酸盐、硅酸盐、钛金属和氚，而玩家发展城市所建造的各类建筑、城市外建设各类设备设施、新建城市等等，对所有的资源的需求量都极为庞大。 资源的获取只有探索获取、建筑生产和星球贸易。 但是，探索需要消耗电力、建造建筑需要大量各类资源、星球贸易的线路增加亦需在城市外建设更多的的设备同样会消耗诸多资源。 有得必有失，因此，玩家必须考虑将每一份资源精打细算，用到正确的地方，逐渐形成资源增长且不影响民众支持度的良性循环。 游戏采用回合制策略形式、点线网状型探索地图模式，让玩家步步为营，逐步实现火星改造的大计划。 每一个回合，玩家能够通过消耗电力，从任一已探索的区域点向下一个点进行线性延伸探索，探索点距离城市越远，消耗电力越多。 不同的探索点，其地形、资源产出也各不相同，这些由电脑在每局初始随机生成。 在平原、熔岩山、环形管这类地形中，还可以建设新的城市，形成新的中心，进一步辐射到火星的四面八方。 玩家将带有问号的未探索点解锁后，可以通过从任一城市向外辐射，逐步占领相邻区域领。 不同城市间的延伸占领线路不能互通且会阻拦，因此，玩家在占领点数有限的情况下，需要合理规划每一座城市延伸出的占领线路避免点数浪费，（占领所需点数则需通过提升城市的人口数量获取）。

candidates.title: April devlog: Changes between the Prologue and Early Access
candidates.text:
As mentioned in the previous devlog, the game now has a goal which is different depending on each scenario. There is no limit to the number of turns you can play but you must reach the goal before your total support reaches 0. Winning a game often takes about 60 to 70 turns. With all the new elements to consider this will usually take a few hours. Some examples of goals are: “fully terraforming the planet” or “getting a specific amount of prestige from spreading life” or “mining a specific amount of resources”... And in addition there are multiple difficulty levels per scenario. This makes replaying the game more varied and provide more interesting challenges.

The new goal bar above your current population support.

We’re very excited that the game will finally release so soon, and would like to thank everybody again for playing the Prologue and supporting us!

See you in a week with the game’s EA release!
Terraf Team

candidates.title: Terraformers review
candidates.text: Well, the usual resource-management. You'll also get resources by exploring the planet.There are different locations for those projects. You have some for cities, others need to be outside the cities and then there's projects in space. You expand your cities by building homes for your people (or robots) and have to take care to get/keep their support.Then there are also leaders you can choose, which give you certain benefits. There's a lot of choices to make in this game. Plus there are also events sometimes, from sandstorms damaging your buildings to golden science years speeding up your research.There's no endless mode currently, you play scenarios which end as soon as you've reached your goal. There are different paths, that have a different focus, and each has multiple difficulties which you unlock by winning easier games.The only thing I'm missing right now is an endless mode, because I didn't really get to do a lot of terrforming yet (I just started my 3rd game). But it's pretty early on the roadmap, so that's gonna be there very soon.I love the art style and how many different kinds of projects there are already and that you unlock even more as you progress. I'm really looking forward to the planned additions, but already have that "just one more turn/game" feeling as it is now.There is a roadmap already, so if you see anything on there you really want, I suggest waiting for a bit. There's also a demo (Prologue) that you can try if you're not sure.Also, the devs are very responsive on Discord, which is usually a good sign.

candidates.title: Tariq Fayed
candidates.text: Tariq's Overwork ability, while sometimes helpfull, has two major drawbacks: 1. it can only be used once per city and 2. with Tariq being an early game leader, the resource gain from the ability is likely to be limited. On the other hand, his Police Station building is great, since it allows to offset early penaltys for Living quality (like low temperatures) and will scale in the later stages of the game if the population of the city is increased. His Specialization, like most early Game Boost specializations has the ability to provide a significant boost in Water production in the end game, especially with water being one of the more readylie available resources later on with some provinicial and oceanic buildings providing large amounts of water.

candidates.title: Terraformers review
candidates.text: Arguably more board game than video game, Terraformers is a turn-based, resource and hand management game in which you establish colonies on Mars with the aim of reaching your chosen scenario goal. The first 25-ish turns are about building up your resource production in the most efficient way possible. You don’t necessarily need everything straight away, but there’re definite priorities you’ll get the gist of after a few games, which unfortunately makes the early game a little repetitive. Once you’ve got some production going then the game lets you get a bit more creative as you decide how you want to pursue the scenario goal.There’re seven scenario types, with increasing difficulty levels for each, though they’re all the same. For instance, the Blue and Green Paths are both terraforming focused, while the Red Path and Expansionist scenarios are expansion themed. As you increase the difficulty then the nuances between each one become more apparent as you’re pressed to play more efficiently, but the different goals are really just shifting your priorities within a given run. For example, in the expansion scenarios you can slack on terraforming and space efforts somewhat, but you’ll still end up doing a small amount eventually because the benefits you get from them are typically still important enough (or even necessary) to warrant some investment. Overall, this can lend runs a same-y feel to them, particularly with how predictably the early game plays out each time.If you can stomach the repetitiveness then there’re a lot of meaty decisions to make, particularly when playing at an appropriate difficulty for your skill. Furthermore, the pacing feels good.

candidates.title: Terraformers review
candidates.text: Terraformers is an... game. I enjoyed it, I think it does a lot of things very well, but it has some rough edges and balance issues.As someone who enjoys 4X games like Civ but doesn't like the combat element, Terraformers is a great experience. There's events you have to grapple with, but none of them involve other empires trying to steal your land and kill your people. In fact, pretty much any hold you solidify remains yours for the entire game. Thus, part of the challenge is strategizing how to proceed in a way that won't undermine your later efforts.One thing Terraformers does that I really appreciated is it injects an almost roguelite element - you have different scenarios with different goals which you can keep ramping up, challenging your own times, and win experience for. The experience unlocks new buildings, projects, and leaders as you go (current cap is level 34). As someone who theoretically to replay Civ as a conqueror or religious leader but keeps getting boxed in, this is a really nice feature. If you want to go greedy resource-grabber mode, there's a challenge for that; one for terraforming, ecology, science, expansion, space projects, etc.The game does have some awkward elements. The constant raising standards for Support applies a natural pressure, but sometimes it can get out of hand with little recourse. Some random events are so resource-intensive that they can change the scope of the game in one turn (ie the Earth crisis, which I pretty much always either take the embargo hit on or just restart). It is pretty easy to get comfortable and never use certain cards. Some effects don't synergize in ways that totally make sense - especially terraforming, I'm confused on why we can only have 1 animal in any zone.

candidates.title: Terraformers review
candidates.text: 游戏存档只能保存当前进度，每次存档都会把之前的存档覆盖。 初入游戏的游玩体验让我觉得有点类似冰汽时代，开局都是在一个坑里，然后生产食物增加人口，在城市周边地点进行探索获取资源，资源用于建设城市内的建筑设施。 特别是开局选领袖时有个人有加班技能（降低民众支持度以换取额外的生产资源），一下就让我把这俩游戏想到了一起。 但玩着玩着发现仅仅是视觉上类似而已，实际玩法差的挺多的。 游戏中不需要考虑时间问题，领袖的探索技能只依靠电力，越远电力需求越大。 探索的资源是马上入库的，即使是人造卫星固定3回合CD，探索的资源也是马上入库的。 游戏中建造设施也是资源够了马上建成，直接投入使用。 这点我玩着觉得蛮不错的。 游戏通关的方法应该还蛮多的，因为决胜点影响因素就很多，只要偏向几个因素大力发展，应该都能过。 我通的这局偏向提高居民支持度，然后资源平衡生产，稍微改造下环境就通了。 游戏不算复杂，像我这种没啥基础的玩一会也能上手。 虽然环境改造的一些东西没搞懂，不过应该只是提供不同方向的通关方法，不影响游玩。 游戏有好几个难度，居民的期望和决胜点要求可以调整的。 我通的倒是最简单的难度。 游戏非常适合打发时间，或者是摸鱼啊，琐碎时间游玩。 有事的时候直接放着不管就好了，暂停都不用。 我的游玩时间20小时左右，抛去挂机的时间，也玩了蛮久的。 1. 游戏的随机事件类型太少了，我玩了3局，基本上见到的随机事件都是火星地震、沙尘暴、探索到别人剩下的补给箱。 好歹是扩殖一个星球欸，随机类型不得多弄一些吗。 科幻性质的来一些2.

candidates.title: Pekai Ayad
candidates.text: While Pekais abilityss allow for an early boost in support income, the impact of them is limited in the long run. The bonus of +3 Support for a building space without adjacency boni is easiely overshadowed by mid to late-stage buildings and the bonus gain of 2 support per turn per new city does not scale well with the later rise in demand, making the Specialization nearly useless in later stages of the game. Her Industrial Lobbying ability gives a small boost of every minable resource, but the resource gain by exploration of a new tile, will in most cases be higher in the net gain of resources and be more targeted towards the resources needed in the current situation, if the neccessary resource is available to explore.

candidates.title: Terraformers review
candidates.text: 这是一款拥有多种玩法内容且带有特色的回合策略游戏，主要是进行火星殖民，之后充分利用火星资源改造火星，把火星改造成另一个美丽的绿色星球，正所谓要想生活过得去，火星就得带点绿~ 领袖是每十年（十回合）换一任且不得连任，每个领袖自带一个探索星球的标准技能和其他两个主动和一个被动专属技能，因此，在有限的回合内发挥该领袖的最大效果才是最重要的。 前期建议先不要选改造基因和提供太空项目的，根本没有能力去用，到第三任领导人再考虑。 选择随机建筑抽卡这一块，优先选择农场或者电场，然后有加成建筑选加成建筑，因为比较难抽。 我有一局，第三个回合没选土壤工厂，然后就再也没见到过了，关于人口建筑的话，个人喜欢优先建设第二座城，然后再扩建人口建筑。 还有建城有条件少选平原，辐射大支持度得的少，沙尘暴坏的东西比较多。 建筑这一方面优先造建筑群，也就是三个或四个资源产出建筑，中间放一个资源加成建筑，如果开局的图只能造一个建筑群的可以重开一把。 一般倾向于优先造电和粮食，科技建筑在第一个城市里一般不造，因为一开始的目的主要是探索和扩张，我到后期他其他资源一般都只有几十的情况下，科技能剩个好几百。 城外一般优先扩张有资源的地方造矿场，然后如果你有望远镜和太阳能电厂也可以选山峰，另外，观光塔少造点，个人感觉稍有一丢丢亏。 区域改造主要是看右边那四个参数，要么完成太空竞赛项目，要么通过放置部分细菌和特定的建筑来进行提升，只有海洋最为特殊。

candidates.title: Terraformers review
candidates.text: Early Access Review - Initial release weekendI encountered NO bugs in over 5 hours of play on a Launch product. STRANGELY SATISFYING.I am reviewing the product as-is, and I imagine it will only get betterThis game is already an excellent play, especially for the price. I play a LOT of strategy games, I own a wall full of board games. This definitely has the feel of a board game, from the technology cards you draw each turn, to the action-based turn play. But it has too much going on to truly track in a board game format. You build up multiple cities, constructing housing, food production, entertainment, and their outlying territories, from exploring for resources, exploiting those resources with mines/observatories/power plants, and managing city comfort. There are also space projects to export resources for (and spaceports for doing so, or for trading with earth). You also have leaders with specialties (like extra water for every 3 water you produce, or extra research benefits for keeping happiness over a certain number), and those specialties last for the whole playthrough. The leaders also have unique actions you can use as your once-per-year/turn action choice.After initial production and a city or two are up and running, you will start terraforming via production of atmosphere, heat, etc. and this affects the regions' base temp, etc. Equator regions start off almost not-freezing, and the poles start off deadly cold. This affects comfort of cities, and which species of bacteria/plant/animal you can introduce to those regions.Hopefully you get the picture, there is a lot to do here already. There is meta-progress, where you unlock some of the more complex buildings/leaders as you finish games, and higher difficulty levels, where the game not only gets harder, but also longer.

candidates.title: Terraformers review
candidates.text: Terraformers is another new Martian colonisation game that is closer to the digital boardgame Terraforming Mars than it is Surviving Mars. I suppose you could call Terraformers a single player boardgame.I love games about Mars - I suspect I've played them all. I like them closer to real science than I do the more imaginative Mars games, such as Per Aspera. I also prefer the more global focus of Terraformers over, say, Surviving Mars. In Terraformers you'll find yourself colonising the whole planet rather than a sector. It is then up to you whether you colonise the world or keep it in its pristine state...or at least as close as with all the mining you'll do.Terraformers is in early access, and it's on of those early access titles that is very playable from the get go - in case the words early access concern you. There's a fully developed roadmap that tantalises what is to come. Right now the game is easy to beat. I beta my first game today and didn't come close to losing. I was actually just setting up to really push terraforming when I suddenly won. I wanted to carry on but that is afeature to come.I got a nice unlockables window when I got to the victory screen. I hadn't realised that the game had this and it does mean that at this early stage there are reasons to keep playing.It is safe to say I am impressed with Terraformers so far. I can't wait to see the game develop. Afterall, I could colonise Mars every day.Now, if only I could actually go there!EDIT: I must add that is was only after going to start a new game that I realised it could get harder than my first go. I am now thinking your 'first game' is kind of an extended tutorial.

candidates.title: Misha Kiyama
candidates.text: Mishas ability to Import Lifeforms can easily Jumpstart the Terraforming process of Mars, since the first Bacteria Spreader is always automatically obtained when the first Bacterium is imported to mars, allowing a head start for bacteriums which raise the temperature or the levels in atmosphere and oxygen. Since early Terraforming can be majorly impacted by the fast spread of bacteria, building multiple bacteria spreaders is a feasable strategy, which is greatly supported by the Specialization. Unfortunately the late game Impact of the Specialization is negligable, since it the bacteria spreaders become nearly obsolete, once the terraforming milestones are reached.

candidates.title: Terraformers review
candidates.text: Ein Strategiespiel dass es sich zur Aufgabe macht eine mögliche Geschichte zu erzählen wie der Mars besiedelt werden könnte. Für ein Early-Access Titel hat es schon einige besondere Features wo jedoch hoffentlich noch andere dazukommen werden. Der einstig in das Spiel ist auch schön gestaltet, man wird nicht mit einer Wucht an Informationen überflutet sondern lernt alle nötigen Infos schritt für schritt und der Anstieg der Komplexität ist genau richtig.Ich würde mir nur wünschen es würde einen größeren unterschied machen welche Spielweiße man wählt. Das Terraforming hat mir zu wenig Einfluss auf die Stats, ich finde auch das die steigende Unzufriedenheit unbelohnend ist, es gibt z.b. keine Möglichkeit die Marsmüdigkeit, trotz noch so viel ähnlichkeit des Marses zur Erde, zu senken. Klar braucht das Spiel auch im späteren Spielverlauf einen Challengefaktor. Aber es sollte meiner Meinung nicht mehr an der Zufriedenheit sondern durch einen neun Faktor wie z.b. an Umweltverschmutzung, Energieknappheit, Nahrungsversorgung die Challenge ins Game kommen. Ebenso ist es unsatisfying dass man den Mars in den Challanges nie bis zum Ende Terraformt, es reicht meist aus 1/5 davon zu Terraformen, oft kommt es auch in den schwierigsten Schwierigkeitsgraden vor dass man gar nicht dazu kommt überhaupt zu beginnen die Fauna zu verteilen, da man schin zuvor gewonnen hat. Das alles sind aber normale Kritikpunkte eines Early-Access Titels und ich bin gespannt was der Entwickler noch daraus zaubern wird.

candidates.title: Terraformers review
candidates.text: Good for an early access game, but there are several frustrating mechanics. 1 is the happiness mechanic, sometimes you just don't get the cards that can boost the happiness leading to an early loss even if you are doing great elsewhere.2 is the ocean level, only being able to increase ocean level by extraction and space project is very annoying. There are several times where I just couldn't get the space project to get the ocean level high enough, causing a green path loss. 3. each round you pick 1 out of 3 potential cards with buildings to give more. I think it should be 1 out of 4 or 5 as the default to reduce the luck involved in the game.

candidates.title: Terraformers review
candidates.text: Terraformers is a great game: intellectually engaging, beautiful, fun, and fluid gameplay.I wouldn't call the game "rogue-like" per se simply because of the random cards and resources; it's a solid resource management game.The only mixed feelings I have about the game is about the difficulty levels - the difficulty ramps quite quickly; the hardest levels are indeed hard, so should provide adequate level of challenge. But the challenge seems to come from two sources: - faster and more brutal penalties from macro factors (pop expectation levels, comfort levels, disasters) - the deck of cards become larger and larger as you progress-> I think the second point is an issue. The mechanics are: as you complete the easier scenarios, you get achievement points that unlock new cards. The problem is that not all new cards are superior than initial cards: some of them are and complement the game nicely (eg building stuff on ocean titles), but others are simply more expensive cards that generate more output (eg the 30+ resource cards). Therefore, at the more challenging levels, you end up have to build your economy and support much faster AND have a lower probability of receiving initial cards that are balanced and needed (eg all the basic +1 resource cards).This is only my hunch by reading the game mechanics; if that is true, this makes the game challenging for a bit frustrating reasons (why am I getting these super expensive cards at the beginning of the game).I'm still playing, so let's see how it progresses. But I'm still having lots of fun w it, so definitely recommend.

We have now shifted our focus towards work on future updates, following our roadmap and specific improvements requested by the players. The features that are planned for the first major Early access update are:

Technologies
Technologies are the aspect of the update that will have the most impact on the gameplay. They are proposed like projects, but only cost science. A technology provides a global benefit that will allow you to specialize your strategy further. Some examples of benefits that technologies can give:

- Artificial intelligence: New robots provide +1 support income
- Enhanced Photosynthesis: Newly planted trees produce double the oxygen and gas.
- Megastructure Construction: When constructing a building that costs at least 40 resources, gain 5 random resources back.

Example of upcoming technology project.

Marsyclopedia
We will also add the first iteration of a “Marsyclopedia” to the main menu. Here, you will find all projects, lifeforms, leaders and locations that you’ve encountered at least once in the game. You can read up on them here and have a good overview, which can help you get a better understanding of the different potential strategies in the game.

Design conceprt of the Marsyclopedia screen.

Custom Mode
This might be our most requested feature since the launch, so we’ve decided to include it in the first major update as well. In custom mode, you’ll be able to set up the game to exactly how you want it by defining the victory condition, expectation rise frequency and severity of damage you’ll receive during the game. You can even choose not to select a victory condition and fully remove expectation rises and damage, allowing you to play a stress-free endless sandbox version of the game. Some mechanics might not hold up in very long runs, but it will be part of the Early Access journey to discover and address that together.

candidates.title: Wartales review
candidates.text: Because of quite positive press around Wartales I probably had too high hopes for it: an emergent story-driven game with moderately complex survival and interesting tactics elements in a somewhat unique medieval world. After playing for two hours of it, I can say Wartales is all of these things, but simply not to the level that is needed. The story does not really emerge due to the relatively flat characters and their unimpactful traits and interpersonal relatons, The survival is robust but not very challenging in itself, only obfuse in its mechanics. The tactics are a solid base but seldom become interesting. There is little room for creativity currently and it is mostly trading blows with opponents that you hopefully outnumber. The world is grittyish, but not really deep beyond standard medieavalist fare.The game looks certainly pretty and all the ingredients are there. There is simply not enough at the level of quality (currently) where I could have fun with it. The quite hefty price tag of 35 euros was enough for me to ask (and get) a refund. I'll certainly consider rebuying it when it has left Early Access and reviews are promising.

candidates.title: Wartales review
candidates.text: This is ABSOLUTELY the sort of game you need to watch a no commentary gameplay video for. Within the first 15 minutes you're either going to love it or find it boring, and that stance is very unlikely to change even after playing dozens of hours. Wartales is fantastic, but it's very niche. If you've been craving a slow paced, grounded, party-based adventure in a low-fantasy world with a heavy focus on trade, inventory management, and exploration then this is your game. However, if any single part of that sounds tedious then the entire game falls apart. Like most games in this genre, there is combat and it's turn-based tactical. It's fun at first, but there's no auto-resolve feature to complete fights so fighting can become tedious on the hardest difficulty. To me, that reinforces the role playing aspect though - roving bands of outlaws should be avoided, not attacked just because it's free XP and loot. If you get tired of combat, you can always lower the difficulty on the fly to make fights a breeze. On the bright side, if you like the bones of the game but there are parts of it that annoy you there are mods available right now. Once you get the hang of it, modding the game yourself is quite simple. The devs are (allegedly) looking to allow Steam workshop support too, so modding could become even better in the future. That really makes a huge difference in a game like this, because there are a lot of things that just weren't quite right for me that the modding tool let me change.

It does suck how the beginning is a grind but in the end that just makes it all the more enjoyable and immersive. As you see your company grow from 4 farm boys with rags and sticks to professional mercenaries with iron plate armor and swords it makes you feel a sense of accomplishment. I did decide to play on region lock so that may be why i had such a hard time (makes different areas have higher or lowers level enemies. other mode has all enemies scale to you). Overall this is a great title that i did not expect to enjoy so much and think it is definitely worth the price tag. I would say some polish needs to be added (mostly with tool tips not going away or company path finding on the map) but a great game none of the less.

candidates.title: Ability Scores (BG3)
candidates.text:
Ability Scores, or Abilities for short, are a game mechanic in Baldur's Gate III. They are basic physical and mental attributes that measure a creature’s capabilities. There are six abilities: Strength, Dexterity, Constitution, Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma.

During Character Creation, Ability Scores are given default values based on the selected class. The player can then redistribute 27 of these points, raising or lowering abilities between a minimum of 8 and a maximum of 15. Raising an ability score by +1 costs 1 point, until it reaches 13 points; raising it above 13 costs 2 points for each +1 increase.

In addition, bonuses of +1 and +2 can be applied to two ability scores, potentially raising them as high as 16 or 17.

The character's Primary Ability is marked with a star, depending on the class's specialty. For spellcasters it's the ability uses for spellcasting; for other classes it's the ability used for melee or ranged attacks.

At Class levels 4, 8, and 12, a character can earn 2 additional points that can be applied to one ability or split between two abilities, to a maximum score of 20.

candidates.text: Re-edit after completing the game/ To start, the art, visuals, and story of this game are pretty good.The main problem I now have with this game is the replay value. Once you've beaten it I fail to see how there could be any more surprises. The story is very linear and there is only the one story, There are however a few different story elements based on choices you make which I think hardly constitutes a full replay. For the price I feel the length of the game is not worth it. I can see why they went with the price though again, it is visually very pretty and the story is good. The time spent isn't strictly always exploring. A lot of it is just sitting around watching a movie while you wait for research points, if you're like me at least. Some things that may bug you as a first time player. I had to restart this game half way through the third chapter because of a bug that was present at launch. They had patched the accident bug but, it didn't seem to be working. As soon as I started a new save, I never got one single accident the entire time from start to finish of the game. Even still, you will most likely end up restarting because there are a few frustrating things that can happen in terms of gameplay that will lead to a spiral of death. Restarting in this game felt terrible because of how long it takes to get back to where you were in the development of the ship.Last real complaint, you are punished harshly for not having meta knowledge of the game. That would be ok but again, restarting feels terrible. Teching back up takes a very long time, even with full upgrades to the tech lab. I would rate this game as a 3/5. I don't think it's purely terrible. It just feels like there could have been more to it than there was.

I saw some behind the scenes director's cut ideas, but sad that they didn't make it to the actual game, as they could've really helped flesh out the story more. Overall, I still enjoyed Borderlands 3 though, despite my frustrations sometimes with the story and how they treated the characters. I also really loveeeed Bounty of Blood dlc. At first I didn't think I would. I thought it would just be another wasteland planet with boring people, but it really changed as I went along and I really loved the whole vibe and unique locations. The art direction, unique settings, and last but not least the characters you can play as were really amazing in B3. I played every character at once! I enjoyed each one and didn't get bored. This was a huge improvement compared to previous games. I also love that more legendary guns were accessible to casual players without excessive grind. Maybe too many, but still, I loved it. Allowed me to have fun as I'm mostly a solo player. I think for future Borderlands game, take the story at its own pace. Keep it fun and amazing with the silly humor, but during sad moments, let the game breathe and take it slow. A good balance of highs and lows really makes a whole lot of difference in story-telling. I really wish B3 had that in its main campaign. But still, overall, I love the game. Looking forward to B4 and hope it's better with a better story and a fun new cast of exciting characters.

candidates.title: Embark on a journey in Cycles Reforged Update!
candidates.text:
Q: The Sealed Biome looks just like a regular biome. Is this intended?
This Update focuses solely on the Cycle overhaul (which is the foundation for any future work). We've been working on the build-up, not the climax (yet). On the journey before destination (sorry/not sorry for the blatant Brandon Sanderson reference).

The current Sealed Biome is just a placeholder and we're already in the middle of designing a proper new biome with unique visuals, music, and a potential mechanic for reforging the Seal. We expect to deliver it in late July or early August (this is, of course, subject to change).

You can see a sneak peek of the new biome above.

Q: Is there any content gated behind difficulty zones?
The World Map is divided into difficulty zones with each Seal marking the border of the particular difficulty. Playing farther away than the zone’s border will require you to play on a higher difficulty.
The aim here is to:

- Encourage players to amp up the difficulty as part of the game’s natural progression.
- Prevent situations when it would be optimal to play the last games in a Cycle (before attempting to close the Seal) on lower difficulties to accumulate negative modifier bonuses.

No actual content is gated behind the difficulty. You can still encounter each of the game’s Modifiers within the Settler difficulty zone.

We consider adding cosmetic rewards for completing Seals in the future. In our conversations with players, this was generally agreed on to be rewarding enough for those who complete them and not a deal-breaker for players who don’t aim to play on higher difficulties. We encourage you to share your thoughts with us too!

candidates.text:
Answer
Havoc is not locked to a specific character, “ergo” Havoc is account-wide. With Havoc our intent is for players to adapt to the Havoc Assignment at hand by selecting the correct character, talents, weapons, blessing and curios to best take on the challenge. Question
Will new garb be also character locked then? (Level up operative to gain access to new Moebian cosmetics for that class).

Answer
The cosmetics from Havoc are account-wide. (The same as any other cosmetic in the game.)

Question
What determines the max difficulty that I can currently play?

Answer
As long as a player is level 30 and can find a group that is willing to take them along, a player could in theory play any Assignment level at any time.

Question
Do I get access to a difficulty, based on my current highest completed? Can I access all difficulties <= my current max, or only 1 diff at a time?

Answer
At all times you have access to your own Assignment. If you feel like playing a lower Assignment level the way to do so would be to find a party with a lower Assignment level in the party finder and vice versa if you are looking for a higher Assignment level than what you currently own.

Question
Does my max available mission difficulty get reset every week?

Answer
Your maximum available mission difficulty will move forward with you into the next week. Each week players will get a new Havoc Assignment based on the highest Assignment they completed the previous week.

Question
Do i need to play from diff 1-40 within a single week in order to get to rank 40, unless i just join someone else's high diff mission?

Answer
No, you will continue the next week at the same level that you left off the previous week. The only thing that is weekly dependent is the weekly reward that is based on the highest-ranked mission you completed during the week.

But Seal Contracts aren’t the only big thing coming in this update. We also bring you 3 brand-new World Events. Fishmen Tribe

Balance-wise, this update brings a whole host of community-inspired tweaks. Most importantly, we decided to change the Prestige 15 difficulty modifier. Instead of prolonging the Storm, it now increases the threshold of Resolve required to generate Reputation after each earned point. However, this doesn’t mean the Storm will become shorter in Prestige games. We simply moved the Storm duration effect to the Viceroy difficulty, making it no longer a Prestige modifier, but a regular stat increase.

Now, why did we do this? Mainly because Storm duration effects are a double-edged sword. On one hand, they make the game harder, as players need to withstand hostile conditions for a longer period. On the other hand, at a certain point, a longer Storm is more of a bonus than a penalty (for example, by prolonging each year and making it easier to achieve certain objectives or postponing Hostility increases). That’s why we decided it would make for a good challenge on earlier difficulty levels, especially considering that a lot of recent updates have introduced various buffs and additional ways of dealing with setbacks, and there was always an effect missing between Veteran and Prestige 1 (both Veteran and Viceroy had the “Blight & Corruption” tag in the Embarkation Panel).

candidates.title: In Stars And Time review
candidates.text: In Stars and Time is, at its core, an RPG that effectively uses a time loop as a metaphor for depression. It's also a lot more than that. While not without some flaws, and aspects that will frustrate some players, I'm glad to have played it and would recommend it to anyone who doesn't mind repetition and backtracking, as long as they're used with purpose.My favorite thing about In Stars and Time is its characters and their dialogue. I genuinely enjoyed each and every one of them, and what they had to say to each other. It's rare that I like a main cast so well, or so quickly into a game (in fact, I fell in love with them back in my time with them in the demo, and at under a half hour into it).The story itself is also a highlight. As I started out by saying, the time loop in the story allowed the game to explore depression. There's the feeling of being trapped as attempts at trying new things lead to the same result with no escape at hand. Siffrin, the protagonist and only member of your party that remembers things from loop to loop, makes the decision to hide that they're looping through time. And this reminded me very much of how there have been times that I've tried to put on a convincing cheery facade at points I've been struggling. And that's just the tip of the iceberg!Besides exploring topics of mental health, the game explores LGBTQ+ themes in ways I appreciated. All of the party is queer in one way or another, and a couple of the characters have their identites explored in meaningful ways.
